Tetris.text: Alexey Pajitnov named it by combining "tetra", meaning four, with his favorite sport, tennis.
Tetris.evidence: The name Tetris was coined by Pajitnov as a combination of "tetra" (meaning "four") and his favorite sport, tennis.

Minecraft.text: Microsoft's $2.5 billion purchase followed a tweet in which creator Notch asked a corporation to buy his stake.
Minecraft.evidence: Originally created by Markus "Notch" Persson using the Java programming language ... On 15 September 2014, Microsoft, the developer behind the Microsoft Windows operating system and Xbox video game console, announced a $2.5 billion acquisition of Mojang, which included the Minecraft intellectual property. Persson had suggested the deal on Twitter, asking a corporation to buy his stake in the game after receiving criticism for enforcing terms in the game's end-user license agreement (EULA), which had been in place for the past three years. According to Persson, Mojang CEO Carl Manneh received a call from a Microsoft executive shortly after the tweet, asking if Persson was serious about a deal.

Grand Theft Auto V.text: Its marketing included a website for a fictional cult, the Epsilon Program, offering fans a spot in the game as members.
Grand Theft Auto V.evidence: They ran a viral marketing strategy with a website for a fictional religious cult, "The Epsilon Program", that offered users the chance to feature in the game as members of the cult.

Red Dead Redemption 2.text: Your outlaw gains or loses weight depending on how much he eats, and his hair grows realistically over time.
Red Dead Redemption 2.evidence: The player can gain or lose weight depending on how much they eat; an underweight character will have less health but more stamina, while an overweight character can better absorb damage but with less stamina. ... The player can bathe to remain clean and visit a barber to change hairstyles; hair grows realistically over time.

Wii Sports.text: After remotes kept flying out of players' hands, Nintendo offered replacement wrist straps almost twice as thick.
Wii Sports.evidence: This string of accidents, and others related to players throwing the Wii Remote while playing Wii Sports, prompted Nintendo president Satoru Iwata to develop a campaign to reduce such incidents. In regard to the issue, Nintendo spokesman Yasuhiro Minagawa commented, "People tended to get a bit excited, especially while playing the game, and in some cases the remote would come loose from their hands." Nintendo responded by offering replacement Wii Remote wrist straps that were almost twice as thick.

Mario Kart 8.text: Nintendo patched an Inkling Girl pose that means "bring it on" in Japan but looks obscene in Europe.
Mario Kart 8.evidence: Shortly after launch, Nintendo released a software update that changed one of the victory gestures done by the Inkling Girl. ... In Japan, the gesture means something similar to "bring it on!", though in European and Latin American countries, it was likened to the bras d'honneur, an offensive gesture

PUBG: Battlegrounds.text: The shrinking safe zone is a circle because Brendan Greene wanted squares but was too new to coding.
PUBG: Battlegrounds.evidence: In taking inspiration from the Battle Royale film, Greene had wanted to use square safe areas, but his inexperience in coding led him to use circular safe areas instead, which persisted to Battlegrounds.

Terraria.text: It came out earlier than planned because a beta version from a closed playtest leaked to the public.
Terraria.evidence: Terraria was released on Steam for Windows on May 16, 2011. This was earlier than planned, since a beta version from a closed playtest had been leaked to the public.

The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.text: One person designed all of Oblivion's dungeons; Skyrim's 150 took a team of eight.
The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.evidence: While just one team member was charged with designing dungeons in Oblivion, Skyrim's 150 dungeons were designed by a group of eight people.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.text: CD Projekt marketed it as "Skyrim in a Game of Thrones sauce".
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.evidence: To achieve the second, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was marketed as "Skyrim in a Game of Thrones sauce".
